subject: mathematics
question_text: Define an even function and an odd function.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.15, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 27. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape is the one this bank uses for a Maths-1A Section A question, and here it also matches the question itself, which asks for two definitions. The condition on the domain, that x ∈ A implies −x ∈ A, is stated in the written lines because without it neither definition can be tested. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. recall_prompt: Say the two definitions in your own words, and give one example of each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define an even function
steps.margin_note: First mark. The examiner reads for the equation f(−x) = f(x) and for the words "for every x in the domain". A bare example earns nothing.
steps.memory_tip: Even means the sign of x does not matter: changing x to −x leaves the value unchanged.
lines: Let A ⊆ R be a set such that x ∈ A ⇒ −x ∈ A.
A function f: A → R is called an EVEN function
if f(−x) = f(x) for every x ∈ A.
For example, f(x) = x² and f(x) = cos x are

recall.must_convey: That f is even when f(−x) = f(x) for every x in a domain that contains −x whenever it contains x.
accept: f is even if f of minus x equals f of x for every x in the domain
changing the sign of x does not change the value
the domain must contain minus x whenever it contains x
x squared and cos x are even functions
f of minus x equals f of x ayithe adi even function
reject: f of minus x equals minus f of x
x cubed and sin x are examples
heard_as: f of minus x equals f of x

steps.why: The condition on A comes first because f(−x) has to exist before it can be compared with f(x). A definition without it is being applied to points that may not be in the domain.
common_mistakes: Writing f(x) = f(x), which is true for every function and says nothing.
Giving only the example x² and never writing the condition f(−x) = f(x).
Leaving out "for every x in the domain", so the definition rests on one value.

steps.label: Define an odd function
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The minus sign on the right is the whole difference from the even case. Add one example, and say that a function may be neither.
steps.memory_tip: Odd means the sign of x carries through to the value: change x to −x and the answer changes sign.
lines: A function f: A → R is called an ODD function
if f(−x) = −f(x) for every x ∈ A,
where A again satisfies x ∈ A ⇒ −x ∈ A.
For example, f(x) = x³ and f(x) = sin x are
A function need not be either: f(x) = x + 1 is

recall.must_convey: That f is odd when f(−x) = −f(x) for every x in the domain, and that a function may be neither even nor odd.
accept: f is odd if f of minus x equals minus f of x for every x in the domain
changing the sign of x changes the sign of the value
x cubed and sin x are odd functions
a function can be neither even nor odd
f of minus x equals minus f of x ayithe adi odd function
reject: f of minus x equals f of x
x squared and cos x are examples
heard_as: f of minus x equals minus f of x

steps.why: The only change from the even definition is the minus sign on the right, and that single sign is what the mark is for. Saying that a function may be neither shows the two definitions are tests, not two groups that every function must belong to.
common_mistakes: Writing f(−x) = −f(−x), which mixes the two sides up.
Claiming every function is either even or odd.
Giving sin x as an even function and cos x as an odd one; the two are swapped.
